answer: Each agent buys a costly plot in a shared garden, staking a signed cipher key into the soil that uniquely binds its hardware to its identity. That cryptographic commitment acts as a signal broadcast to every peer: a new sprout can only blossom if someone paid real energy and time to tend it. Because farming multiple plots requires multiplying those genuine costs, opening hundreds of fake identities becomes as exhausting as digging a hundred separate fields, so the crowd of plausible agents stays rooted and honest.
